claims.statement: Viewer3D caps Ember's orbit distance at 25 metres.

The Columnar Furnace sits within one continuous exterior-scale volcanic basin while a distant vent and open lava channel establish far depth outside the 4.5 m action radius without forming a uniform enclosure.
Blue-black basalt and rough obsidian dominate the frame; orange is confined to fissures and the banked, crusted river, with restrained mineral ochre as a secondary accent.

exemptions.name: vertical-section
exemptions.rationale: Ember is an orbit backdrop with no traversable vertical route; the four-camera composition board proves vertical scale for this gate.

exemptions.name: route-storyboard
exemptions.rationale: Viewer3D supplies a free orbit rather than a player navigation route; the locked camera board covers the intended visual sequence.

exemptions.name: walkability
exemptions.rationale: Ember is not a walkable museum room; performer action clearance and orbit sightlines are the relevant spatial checks.

exemptions.name: graybox-glb
exemptions.rationale: The Blender topology comparison was the review artifact; runtime GLB proof is deliberately reserved for the approved production-slice gate.

exemptions.name: first-person-walk
exemptions.rationale: Viewer3D is evaluated by orbit cameras rather than first-person navigation; the four-camera contact sheet is the equivalent review proof.

exemptions.name: route-duration
exemptions.rationale: There is no authored player route in an orbit backdrop.

exemptions.name: sequence-parity
exemptions.rationale: This environment slice does not select or modify any TKA sequence.

exemptions.name: state-persistence
exemptions.rationale: Ember is a stateless Viewer3D environment. It introduces no room-owned interaction state to save or restore; performer and playback state remain owned by the shared viewer.

exemptions.name: typecheck
exemptions.rationale: The repository-wide check is baseline-red outside Ember. Gate 6 records all 455 errors and 29 warnings, confirms zero EmberScene or ObsidianPlatform diagnostics, and identifies the two Viewer3D diagnostics as the pre-existing Threlte layers typing mismatch rather than stage-sizing behavior.

regressions.reason: The adversarial review found that technical acceptance did not meet the approved gorgeous-scene art bar. Hero geometry, material separation, atmosphere, and all-angle composition require new registered 3D visual targets.

Gate 4 runtime review showed every performer facing backstage. The shared Viewer3D same-direction formation heading disagreed with its negative-Z audience camera, and cast changes restored the wrong heading.

The adversarial Gate 4 review found an organ-pipe silhouette, neon-zipper fissure, procedural horizontal texture bands, interface-like emissive lozenges, and weak rear-orbit coordination. Revision 4 keeps the same capability owner and rebuilds its art language around geological mass, negative space, occluded heat, and a complete coordinated orbit.
preserved: existing runtime asset and readiness owners

regressions.reason: R6 solved environmental continuity but still read as procedural graybox geology. R7 preserves that continuous spatial chassis and replaces the focal geological language with three audited Meshy multiview modules.
preserved: R6 continuous 380 by 335 m volcanic country

checks.name: camera-registration
checks.evidence: The report records one shared ten-camera set used unchanged by all three Blender target scenes: eight orbit sectors, one geological detail, and one orthographic plan view.

checks.name: silhouette-read
checks.evidence: The comparison and three orbit boards show three distinct hero silhouettes under matched camera and lighting conditions without depending on a pre-existing hero model.

checks.name: action-clearance
checks.evidence: All target geometry and secondary geology remain outside the preserved 4.5 m unobstructed performer action radius, confirmed by the registered plan views.

checks.name: registered-source-provenance
checks.evidence: The R7 report records four unique Ember Meshy multiview source chains, including geometry, retexture, and official remesh task IDs. Each selected source is embedded once; no Ocean asset or unrelated pre-existing hero is present.

checks.name: anti-repetition
checks.evidence: R7 uses one hero escarpment, one collapsed lava bank, one fumarole talus, and one breached distant caldera, then buries each unique source into the continuous R6 terrain. Procedural secondary column clusters and the pyramid-like distant vent were removed after review exposed their graybox repetition.

checks.name: action-clearance
checks.evidence: Computed minimum structural radial clearance is 6.156 m against the preserved 4.5 m performer action radius.

checks.name: performance
checks.evidence: The optimized R7 asset is 6.33 MiB with Meshopt, mesh quantization, and 18 KTX2 textures. The source artifact is 196,906 triangles and its largest mesh is 49,345 triangles.

checks.name: interaction-state
checks.evidence: The shared stage owner grew through one, two, three, and four performers; the corrected four-performer runtime proof keeps every body inside the platform and every visible front toward the audience camera.

checks.name: front-stage-facing
checks.evidence: The Viewer3D formation adapter resolves same-direction layouts to Math.PI for the negative-Z audience camera while preserving explicit back-to-back and inward-facing slots. The corrected hero, four-performer, and seven-viewport proofs show visible chests and props toward camera.

checks.name: runtime-console
checks.evidence: The decisive 1920 by 1080 front-stage runtime capture loaded the final R7 GLB, reached the environment-ready state, and produced no browser-console errors or warnings.

checks.name: focused-verification
checks.evidence: The focused R7 request-safety, provenance, terrain, stage, and shipping-asset suite passed 15 checks with one historical integrated-room todo. Svelte-check completed with zero errors and zero warnings.

checks.name: volcanic-world-composition
checks.evidence: The R6 380 by 335 m terrain owner remains intact. R7's registered eight-sector orbit and decisive runtime view add a fractured columnar landmark, collapsed bank, fumarole talus, and low breached caldera without restoring a uniform enclosure or isolated backdrop.

checks.name: lava-river
checks.evidence: A shared seventeen-point downhill channel drives the static levees and runtime indexed spline surface from the distant vent through the audience side of frame while remaining outside the action radius.
